title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle fleet's battery management system failed to account for extended periods of immobility in heavy traffic. Multiple Waymo vehicles became stranded during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco after sitting stationary long enough to fully deplete their batteries. The deployment assumed vehicles would maintain sufficient charge for their operational scenarios, but did not appear to plan for how the system would behave when caught in severe, unplanned gridlock following a public event.

The failure occurred in the vehicle operation phase, where drained cars required towing and created further traffic obstruction. This would have been caught by stress testing the battery model against historical traffic data for high-volume event scenarios in the deployment region, or by implementing a charging or repositioning protocol when the system detected prolonged stationary conditions and declining battery levels.

One vehicle also caught fire after driving through fireworks set off in the street, though it is not established whether the fire originated in the battery, powertrain, or another component. The incident shows that the system was deployed in an urban environment during high-traffic periods without failsafes designed specifically for public events and the unpredictable hazards they create.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded after their batteries drained while sitting in severe traffic following a fireworks display at the Golden Gate Bridge. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off in the street, though no injuries were reported. A passenger described the car starting to drive while fireworks were being lit nearby.

The incident prompted strong reactions from frustrated motorists, with some people yelling at the driverless cars stuck in traffic. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its ability to handle major traffic disruptions. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office said it will meet with public and private partners to improve traffic management for future events following the approximately 100,000 people in the area that night.
